newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram considers Left budget demands.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram considers Left budget demands.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Tuesday told leaders of four powerful left-wing parties he would examine their demands for changes to his pathbreaking 1997/98 budget.
"I have heard their views. Let us see how much we can accommodate, how many suggestions are acceptable. We will examine it," Chidambaram told Reuters after a two-hour meeting.
"I told them I will do my best to consider their points of view."

The leaders of the four parties, a powerful bloc within Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's United Front coalition, said they objected to proposals on insurance, duties and taxes on personal income and dividends in the budget for the April-March fiscal year.
"I see no major changes in the finance minister's position on major issues," said Biplab Dasgupta, a leader of the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPM), after the meeting.
"On individual items like small industries and some import items he is interested to look into the issues."
Asked whether left-wing parties would move amendments to the budget in parliament if Chidambaram did not accept their suggestions, Dasgupta said: "That we have not decided."
The four parties have 52 deputies in the 542-seat lower house of parliament, where the United Front controls 178 seats.
Chidambaram has proposed reducing the tax rate on annual personal income between 40,000 rupees ($1,115) and 60,000 rupees to 10 percent from 15 percent.
The tax rate on income between 60,000 and 150,000 rupees would be cut to 20 percent from 30 percent, while the rate on incomes above 150,000 rupees would be reduced to 30 percent from 40.
Under Chidambaram's budget proposal, shareholders would be exempted from a tax on dividends.
"The highest slab of tax should be 40 percent and the dividend tax should be imposed," CPM lawmaker Nirmal Kanti Chatterjee said as he entered the meeting.
"We are opposed to insurance privatisation, and in customs and excise duties there should be a thorough review," Chatterjee said.

The lower house of parliament was expected to begin discussing the Finance Bill, which contains tax and tariff proposals for 1997/98, on Wednesday. Voting on the package is expected by the end of the week.
"I will move the Finance Bill tomorrow," Chidambaram said.
Gujral last week promised to hold discussions with major political parties on the proposals before parliament voted on the bill. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
